diagnosis: Customer upgraded to Business mid-cycle on the 14th and their first invoice post-upgrade (INV-88213) is higher than the listed plan price. This matches the standard proration behavior where remaining days on the old plan are credited and a new charge for the upgraded plan is combined into one invoice. Customer is asking for explanation of extra lines, not disputing the charge.
reply: Thanks for reaching out about invoice INV-88213 following your upgrade to Business. When a plan is upgraded mid-billing cycle, the first invoice after the change includes a prorated credit for any remaining days on your previous plan, plus a charge for the new Business plan from the upgrade date. This produces a combined invoice that can look different from the standard list price on its own. The extra lines you're seeing are the proration adjustments, and this only affects the first invoice after your upgrade — subsequent invoices will reflect the regular Business plan rate. You can review the line-item breakdown in your billing portal to see the credit and new charge separated out.
